edit.description: runFanout's per-entry ShipContext.gateResults (~2237) splices the wave-cumulative mergeGateResults accumulator (~1995, declared once outside the perEntry loop and never reset) instead of just this entry's own gate results — scope per entry, e.g. slice mergeGateResults from an index captured before this entry's own afterMerge gate loop runs.
A multi-entry fanout wave whose phase.shipped predicate inspects gateResults sees only that entry's own afterCommit+afterMerge results, never an earlier-processed sibling's afterMerge results.

summary: runFanout's per-entry ShipContext.gateResults leaks every earlier wave entry's afterMerge gate results into each subsequent entry's ship classification.

per.section: Ship detection trusts the agent's own account

tests: a fanout wave's second (and later) entry's ShipContext.gateResults contains only that entry's own gate results, never an earlier-processed sibling entry's afterMerge results
acceptance: phase.shipped's ShipContext.gateResults for entry N in a wave is exactly entry N's own afterCommit+afterMerge results — never includes any earlier-processed sibling entry's afterMerge results.
notes: Sweep finding (posture pass over src/Dispatcher.ts, engineering.md 'Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source'): mergeGateResults is a single wave-level accumulator never reset per entry, contradicting Phase.ts's ShipContext.gateResults docstring ('this entry's own gate results'). Untested — the sole phase.shipped test in Dispatcher.test.ts is single-entry, so the leak is currently invisible.
